content.text:
I fixed `worker.RunAll` so it always writes one complete, valid `out/results.json`. A new test fails on the old code and passes on the new code, including under `-race`.

**Cause:** both workers kept rewriting the same file at the same time. Each one read the file, added one result and wrote the whole file back. When their steps overlapped, one worker's write wiped out the other's results, or one read a half-written file. Because `_ = json.Unmarshal` ignored errors, that broken file was then treated as empty and overwritten, which lost even more results.

**Fix (`worker/worker.go`):** the workers no longer share the file.
- Each worker puts its results into its own positions in an in-memory list, so the workers have nothing in common and need no lock.
- After both finish, `RunAll` writes the file once. It writes to a temporary file in `out/` and then renames it into place, so anyone reading the file sees either the old version or the new one, never a partial write.
- Errors are now returned instead of ignored. It also creates `out/` if it's missing; before, a missing directory made it fail silently.
- Results are now in the same order as the input jobs. Before, the order depended on timing.

**Test (`worker/worker_test.go`):** it runs `RunAll` twice with 200 jobs, then checks that the file is valid JSON, has exactly 200 results, and has the right first and last entries.

**One behaviour change you should know about:** the old code added each run's results to whatever was already in the file, so results built up across calls. Now each run replaces the file with only that run's results. I assumed the build-up across runs wasn't intended, because it meant one run's corrupted file could damage every run after it. If you do want results kept across runs, `RunAll` can load the existing file once before the workers start.
